subject: Observability add-ons: split billing scenarios & sample invoice
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Jamie Ortiz <jamie@brightline.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 13 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Observability add-ons: split billing scenarios & sample invoice

Hi Jamie —

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. Per our conversation I've sketched two invoice scenarios for the observability add-ons (retention, tracing, advanced dashboards) so you can see how the bill would flow depending on the storage mix Brightline expects. Attached: a PDF with line-item invoices and an XLSX with the pricing worksheet.

High-level:
- Scenario A (Hotpath-first): heavy hotpath retention (30d hot + 365d cold), continuous tracing enabled, dashboards charged per seat + query credits. This optimizes for low-latency access but increases tier-1 storage costs.
- Scenario B (Archive-first): most telemetry routed to archival cold storage with on-demand hotpath retrieval (shorter hot window). Lower monthly recurring cost but higher egress/retrieval risk for burst queries.

Numbers in the attachments show monthly and amortized annual costs, plus an optional 12-month commit path where we can offer a bundle discount. A few ask items so we can make the recommendation tighter:
1) Estimated average daily hot ingest (GB/day) and % of traces kept in hot cache beyond 7 days.
2) Typical dashboard concurrency / number of power users (for seat vs query-credit math).
3) Whether Brightline wants a single invoice or split invoices for compute (tokens/ingest) vs storage.

If you prefer, Ben can put together a sample invoice with your exact usage numbers and a comparison row for a 10% bundle discount vs pay-go.

Thanks —
Olga
Director, Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: BRG-3421-sample-invoice-line-items.pdf (PDF stub), obs-addons-pricing-worksheet.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

Hi Olga —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the attachments. A few quick clarifications from Brightline's side:
- Hot ingest is currently ~120GB/day; we expect spike behavior (3x) during batch reconcile windows about twice / month.
- Traces: roughly 40% of traces are actively inspected beyond 7 days; the remainder is archived.
- Dashboards: 12 power users, ~40 total dashboard users who run ad-hoc queries.

Two asks: can you show a sample invoice where billing is split into (1) retention/storage and (2) dashboard/query usage? Our finance team prefers separate lines for storage so it matches internal chargebacks. Also, what's the process/lead time if we accept a 12-month commit and want to apply a one-time migration credit?

Thanks —
Jamie

Jamie / Olga —

Thanks for the details, Jamie — that's super helpful. I've put together a sample invoice (attached PDF) that splits charges across three buckets: Storage (hot vs cold), Tracing (per-trace unit), and Dashboards (seat + query credits). Headline options we're able to offer: 

Option 1: Pay-as-you-go (baseline). No commit. Monthly line items as detailed in the invoice.
Option 2: 12-month commit (recommended for predictability). If Brightline commits to a $120k ARR minimum for observability add-ons we can apply a 10% bundle discount across storage + tracing and grant a one-time migration credit equal to one month's expected storage charge (applied on first invoice).
Option 3: Pilot + volume carveout. 3-month pilot with reduced seat fees (first 3 months at 50% off) then auto-convert to Option 2 if you opt-in.

Per your finance ask: we can produce two invoice PDFs or a single consolidated invoice with split sections. For internal chargeback you said you prefer separate lines — we'll include a CSV export of line-item mapping.

I also included an amortization example in the XLSX showing how the migration credit affects the first quarter. If you want legal-friendly wording for the migration credit / SOW we can drop a one-paragraph clause in the SOW (attached BRG-SOW-draft.docx).

Next steps: if you confirm Option 2 or Option 3 I can draft a short appendix for the SOW and loop in legal. If you want to tighten the numbers I'll re-run the worksheet with 120GB/day + 3x reconcile spikes plugged in.

Cheers,
Ben
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Looping in a quick technical recommendation from our side — attaching my notes inline.

> On Mon, Jun 14, 2027 at 10:15 AM Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai> wrote:
> > Option 2: 12-month commit ... apply a one-time migration credit equal to one month's expected storage charge

That migration credit approach is workable. A couple of technical guardrails to make the billing predictable:
- Recommend a hotpath retention of 30 days for traces and metrics with a hot cache sized to handle your 3x reconcile spikes (we can cap continuous caching at 2x normal ingest and gate bursts to on-demand retrieval to avoid indefinite hot costs).
- Archive (cold) lifecycle after 30d with a 365d cold retention TTL for compliance. Retrieval from cold storage will be billed as retrieval/egress credits — we'll show two price points in the sample invoice (standard retrieval vs expedited retrieval).
- Dashboards: for Brightline's usage mix (12 power users, 40 occasional users) the seat+query credits combo will be ~more economical than seat-only at current query volumes; I'll run the exact projection.

If Brightline goes with the 12-month commit we can include a one-time migration credit and add a 90-day usage cap to avoid surprise egress costs during onboarding (we'll surface any overages weekly during the first 90 days).

Happy to schedule a short call to walk through the invoice lines and the XLSX projections.

— Karthik
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
